chunks: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn Sa'id ibn Qalbuwayh al-Mu'addal in al-Rafiqah narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Kathir al-Tamimi al-Yamani narrated to us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Harb al-Hilali, the emir of Medina, say: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) say:
Wellness is a hidden blessing -- when you have it, you forget about it; and when you lose it, you remember it.

key_terms.العافية: Al-'Afiyah: wellness, well-being, good health and safety from affliction. In Islamic theology, it encompasses physical health, spiritual safety, and divine protection from trials.
key_terms.خفية: Khafiyyah: hidden, concealed, subtle. Describes how this blessing operates below the threshold of conscious awareness.
key_terms.نعمة: Ni'mah: a blessing or favor from God. One of the central Quranic concepts (mentioned over 100 times).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about wellness and gratitude for blessings?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the paradoxical nature of wellness (al-'afiyah): it is a divine blessing that goes unnoticed while present but becomes keenly felt once lost. This teaching, transmitted through a chain including Muhammad ibn Harb al-Hilali, the governor of Medina, emphasizes the importance of gratitude for God's blessings before they are taken away.
